FAST

TOKYO, Nov 10 : The recent volatile swings in global markets are putting greater attention on the Bank of Japan's assessment of financial conditions, a key component of its policy framework that could sway the pace and timing of interest rate increases. With markets returning to some measure of calm after a steep selloff in AI stocks, many analysts expect the BOJ to keep raising interest rates, with the next hike projected to come as soon as December. But the recent rout has tested the central bank's view that brisk AI demand will underpin the economy, with the wealth effect from booming stock prices giving households and companies more spending power. It has also put the spotlight on the BOJ's financial conditions language, which serves as a key gauge of how close its policy rate is to levels deemed neutral to the economy, thus offering clues on the pace and timing of rate rises.

While the BOJ's escalating warning over inflation risks has preoccupied market participants, the less discussed guidance on financial conditions may increase in prominence if the AI market rout keeps equity prices on a downtrend, some analysts say. "The BOJ's basic view is that financial conditions remain loose, which won't immediately change just because stock prices are falling," said former BOJ official Tetsuya Inoue, who is now executive economist at Sony Financial Group. "But if asset prices remain unstable, it may hurt growth by cooling corporate mood and spending from households with stock holdings. Depending on market moves, it could give the BOJ reason to put off a rate hike in December." STOCK WEALTH EFFECT The BOJ has stressed the need to continue raising interest rates to counter upside price risks and prevent underlying inflation from overshooting its 2 per cent target. It has also justified rate hikes by saying financial conditions are loose, pointing to low real borrowing costs, strong corporate funding demand and rising bank lending. While describing interest rates and funding indicators as key measurements, the BOJ said it also looks at asset prices in gauging financial conditions since stock prices and exchange rates affect household and corporate spending. "For example, the uptrend in stock prices likely contributed to a decline in firms' cost of capital and helped support private consumption through wealth effects," the BOJ said in its quarterly outlook report released last month. Such a positive cycle might go into reverse if the stock market adjustment persists and hits Japan's once risk-averse households, who have recently piled into stocks to ride the AI boom. Japanese households' stock holdings reached 486 trillion yen ($3.08 trillion) in June, BOJ data showed, up 47 per cent from year-earlier levels, accounting for 19.3 per cent of their total wealth. "The stock wealth effect is small compared with the US, but could have a sizeable impact on consumption as many in the younger generation now hold stocks," said Seisaku Kameda, the BOJ's former top economist, who is an economist at Japan's Sompo Institute Plus. At last month's policy meeting, the BOJ said financial conditions remained accommodative "in light of recent developments in asset markets," as well as data showing still-low real rates and funding costs. But a summary of opinions from the October meeting, released on Tuesday, exposed a rift in how board members viewed the prevailing financial conditions, with some seeing little impact of past rate hikes, while others warned of the potential hit to growth. In a sign of the board's increased attention, one member called for assessing financial conditions using three measurements: the real interest rate gap, corporate finance and the bank lending channel, and asset prices. "Asset prices, in particular, are affected not only by monetary policy but other factors," as seen in rising stock prices driven by AI-related demand, the member said. For now, markets will be on the lookout for how Governor Kazuo Ueda will describe the impact of the market rout on financial conditions in a speech due on November 30, which precedes the BOJ's next policy meeting on December 17 and 18. "Theoretically, if stock prices fall, that would tighten financial conditions," a source familiar with the BOJ's thinking said, a view echoed by another source. The sources spoke on the condition of anonymity as they were not authorised to speak publicly. "There's still some time before the December meeting," a third source said. "Nobody knows how markets would be behaving then." ($1 = 158.0000 yen)

Source: Reuters

TOKYO, Nov 10 : The Bank of Japan estimates that its accelerated sales of exchange-traded fund (ETF) holdings will generate about 1 trillion yen ($6.33 billion) in additional annual proceeds, Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said on Tuesday. Katayama's remarks come after Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi unveiled plans last week to tap proceeds from the BOJ's ETF sales to fund investment in areas deemed vital to Japan's economic security, as the government seeks new revenue sources without relying excessively on debt issuance. The BOJ decided on October 30 to increase annual sales of its ETF holdings to 860 billion yen from 330 billion yen on a book-value basis. A portion of net profit the central bank reaps each year, including from the ETF sales, is paid to state coffers. "The BOJ has indicated additional proceeds of roughly 1 trillion yen, but the exact amount that will be remitted to the government will depend on fiscal year-end calculations and budget procedures, so we can't say precisely how much it will be," Katayama said.

FAST

NEW DELHI, Nov 10 : Oil prices fell on Tuesday, adding to the previous day's losses after US President Donald Trump downplayed the need for military action against Iran "at this point", easing fears of sustained supply disruptions in the Middle East. Brent crude futures declined 70 cents, or 0.75 per cent, to $91.88 a barrel by 0246 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) futures fell 78 cents, or 0.90 per cent, to $86.07 a barrel. Both benchmarks had fallen 1 per cent earlier in the session. Brent settled down 5.85 per cent in the previous session after sliding to its lowest since August 31. Trump said on Monday he plans to hold off on new military strikes against Iran for the time being after appeals from countries in the region, including from Qatar's prime minister in White House talks.

Trump, in a Reuters interview and a later appearance in the White House press briefing room, said he plans to keep up a naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz for now. "The market continues to prioritise President Trump's more conciliatory tone toward Iran since the midterms," said Tim Waterer, chief market analyst at KCM Trade. "While attacks on shipping around the Strait of Hormuz are still occurring, they have not escalated in a way that has forced a fresh risk premium into the market," he said. On the supply side, OPEC oil output rose in October, a Reuters survey found, led by gains in Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Iraq despite continued constraints on exports. Brent has retreated about 22 per cent from the six-month high of $118 it touched on October 30 as fears that Trump might step up attacks on Iran following the US midterms have eased, however there is still concern shipping could be disrupted. "Despite the recent selloff, prices are unlikely to fall below $90 per barrel for Brent without more durable signs of de-escalation and a US-Iran deal," Gregory Brew, a senior analyst with Eurasia Group said in a note. "At the same time, risks to shipping remain high, as Iran continues to attack vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz," Brew said. Elsewhere, Russian and Ukrainian officials planned to meet on Tuesday for two days of US-brokered talks — their first since February — after Trump suggested last week that a broad peace deal was possible in their 4-1/2-year-old war and could incorporate Europe's security.

Source: Reuters

Nov 9 : Details of Anthropic’s blockbuster IPO, including plans by the AI company to raise nearly $70 billion, were briefly circulated to banks before being retracted late on Monday, according to emails seen by Reuters. A representative of Anthropic sent a copy of a securities filing that showed it aimed to sell about 867 million shares at a price range of $70 to $80 per share, then followed up with an email saying details about the pricing were inaccurate. Anthropic said in the second email it would update the filing later. Anthropic declined to comment. The email did not specify to bankers what was erroneous, and Reuters was unable to determine what was incorrect. The original email whose details were retracted showed Anthropic planned to sell 866.7 million Class A shares, including a secondary offering. Anthropic itself would sell about 843.3 million shares, while existing shareholders would sell an additional 23.3 million shares. The IPO would raise $69.3 billion at the top of the range.

Separately, the original filing showed that Anthropic had lined up $26 billion in investments from some of the world’s biggest technology companies alongside its IPO, underscoring the increasingly intertwined financial ties underpinning the AI boom. Alphabet's Google, Nvidia, Advanced Micro Devices, Broadcom, Micron Technology, Microsoft and TSMC had agreed to participate in the private placement of Anthropic’s Class N common stock at the IPO price, which would close immediately after the IPO, the original filing showed. Anthropic is expected to formally launch the roadshow on Tuesday, with pricing expected in the following week. The Anthropic IPO comes at a time when other companies in the AI infrastructure and data center sectors have delayed or withdrawn their planned listings, facing a rise in interest rates that has helped fuel a punishing selloff in shares and bonds of AI operators such as CoreWeave Inc and broader questions about the sustainability of AI spending.  Investors had previously discussed a valuation of as much as $2 trillion for Anthropic, but expectations have since come down, with the $1.5 trillion figure viewed as the high end of the range, Reuters previously reported. Founded in 2021 by former OpenAI executives including Amodei and his sister Daniela Amodei, who is now Anthropic's president, Anthropic has emerged as one of the leading generative AI developers with its Claude family of models. The company's rapid growth has been underpinned by Google and Amazon, which are simultaneously investors, suppliers of computing power and important distribution partners, as well as AI competitors. Anthropic had nearly $900 billion in computing commitments with partners including Amazon and Google, underscoring how its rapid growth depends on vast amounts of future capacity, some of it reliant on financing beyond the company's control. Anthropic's quarterly growth rate has declined sharply even though revenue stood at almost $17 billion for the three months ended September 30, the company revealed in an amended filing earlier in the month.

Source: Reuters

FAST

SYDNEY, Nov 10 : The dollar found support following a bumpy few days and held firm in Tuesday's Asia session while traders waited for US inflation data, which could push it higher if it bolsters rate hike bets. A tumble in oil prices and gains overnight for stocks had knocked the dollar lower as investors rotated back into riskier assets. The trade and sentiment-sensitive Australian dollar rose by nearly 1 per cent through Monday to sit at $0.6921 early on Tuesday and the New Zealand dollar rose even further to trade at $0.5624, with both steady in morning Asia trade. The euro jumped 0.7 per cent overnight to $1.1220, reversing a Friday fall when strong US jobs data lifted the dollar and interest rate expectations, and putting the euro/dollar pair roughly into the middle of a range it has held for a month.

The market is long dollars and the dollar index has gained this year as early expectations for US interest rate cuts quickly turned to bets on hikes after the US-Israeli war on Iran drove up energy prices and fuelled inflation. A blowout October jobs report on Friday, with hiring more than twice forecasts, has markets pricing an 85 per cent chance of a Federal Reserve rate increase next month. US CPI AWAITED Headline inflation is seen picking up to 3.9 per cent and core to 2.8 per cent, year-on-year, in October, according to economists polled by Reuters, so anything hotter than that will add to rate hike expectations and probably lift the dollar, analysts said. "You can only put a little bit more (in the price) in December, but the price for meetings into the future could go higher," said Imre Speizer, strategist at Westpac in Auckland. Markets have priced two US hikes by the middle of next year, though the outlook has dimmed somewhat amid the recent turbulence in AI stocks on fears a Democratic sweep of Congress could lead to tighter regulation and slow the AI boom. "This could be a factor that slows US growth in 2027 and helps put a top in for the dollar," said Macquarie strategists Thierry Wizman and Gareth Berry in a note to clients. Sterling, which has drawn support since the Bank of England hiked interest rates for the first time in three years last week, sat in the middle of a range it has traded in for almost a year and a half at $1.3441. Japan's yen hovered at 157.97 per dollar, having been the best-performing G10 currency against the greenback over the past six months on the back of heavy official intervention. Figures on Monday showed Japan sold $97 billion in reserves defending the yen through late July and August as it traversed four-decade lows on the dollar. The threat of further dollar sales is keeping the currency steady, even as expectations for a December rate hike in Japan have lately faded.

Source: Reuters

Nov 9 : Trump Media & Technology Group swung to a third-quarter profit on Monday, while its revenue more than tripled from a year earlier, fueled by growth in its Truth API data-licensing business. Shares of the company rose about 1 per cent in extended trading. Founded by US President Donald Trump and known for its Truth Social platform, Trump Media & Technology Group has increasingly sought to transform itself from a social media company into a broader technology and investment business. The company, which is in the process of merging with TAE Technologies in a pivot toward fusion energy, reiterated that the $6-billion deal would close in the current quarter.

Earlier this year, Trump Media launched Truth API, describing it as a subscription-based data feed that provides licensed, low-latency access to publicly available Truth Social posts. Truth API and the Truth+ streaming platform together added $1.8 million in subscription revenue, accounting for the bulk of the company's revenue growth. Revenue soared 205 per cent to $3.0 million in the quarter ended September 30. Last month, Reuters reported that Truth Social has signed Bloomberg, Susquehanna International Group and Jump Trading as customers, with subscribers paying between $60,000 and $100,000 a month for faster access to Truth Social posts. Trump Media shares have fallen nearly 70 per cent this year, including a roughly 32 per cent decline since Democrats won control of the House and Senate in the midterm elections, results widely seen as a rebuke of Trump's policies. "While the market was trading on headlines, the underlying business didn't flinch," interim CEO Kevin McGurn said on a post-earnings call. "Our balance sheet didn't change from Tuesday to Wednesday. Our product traction didn't reverse." The company recorded $409.7 million in net income, driven largely by gains on its cryptocurrency holdings and related securities. This compared to a net loss of $54.8 million a year earlier.

Nov 9 : SpaceX is planning a roughly $24 billion gas-fired power plant and super-compute facility in Starbase, Texas, according to a public hearing notice. The rockets-to-AI company's request comes as opposition to data centers grows, with voters rejecting them in 40 of 41 local ballot measures and Democrats, some of whom had campaigned on pausing new projects, taking control of the US Congress and the Texas governor's office in the midterm elections. The filing shows SpaceX, which bought Elon Musk's AI lab xAI earlier this year, has applied for a property tax abatement for the project. The Starbase City Commission will consider the abatement, plus a related economic development agreement, at a public meeting on December 9. The notice describes $24 billion as the estimated capital investment for the project's initial phases. It said the work may be done in multiple phases and could include future expansions.

It also gave no details on the plant's generating capacity or the scale of the computing operation. SpaceX affiliate Lone Star Mineral Development has filed plans for an 8-mile natural gas pipeline to Starbase, called Starpipe, that is scheduled for service by January 2027. It will feed a planned plant to turn the gas into liquid methane for Starship rockets, according to filings Reuters reviewed in June. BRUSSELS, Nov 9 : Companies found guilty of using unfair digital trade practices to push people to buy more or target children with personalised advertising risk fines of as much as 6 per cent of annual global turnover, according to a European Commission draft law seen by Reuters. The Commission's Justice chief Michael McGrath will present the proposed legislation known as the Digital Fairness Act (DFA) on Wednesday, which will need to be thrashed out with EU countries and the European Parliament before it can become law. The DFA is the latest legislative push by Europe to get Big Tech, e-commerce and social media giants to do more to police content on their platforms. It would ban so-called business-to-consumer "dark patterns" — deceptive or manipulative interface designs on websites and apps that steer people into buying more — as unfair commercial practices, the document said.

Companies using dynamic pricing, where ticket prices fluctuate based on real-time demand and which has triggered criticism from consumers, will be required to be more transparent by disclosing the number of items available at the advertised price. Traders will have to give users the opportunity to switch off addictive features that encourage compulsive or excessive use, the document said. Finance Watch, which campaigns for the public interest in financial services rulemaking, said the proposed legislation does not do enough to protect consumers investing online. "The proposals on dark patterns go in the right direction, but they lack ambition to sufficiently protect consumers in financial services," said Peter Norwood, senior research and advocacy officer at Finance Watch.

Nov 9 : On the streets of Taipei and Seoul, fans of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang mob him for autographs on books, posters and sometimes even on their bodies. In private, even billionaires Larry Ellison and Elon Musk were once reduced to "begging" for his coveted AI chips. The star power that 63-year-old Huang draws as the gatekeeper to Nvidia's chips shows how badly the AI industry is leaning on him for the graphics processing units that train models and run services such as ChatGPT. But he is not just a chip supplier; instead Nvidia has in recent years turned its swelling cash pile into a war chest to fund companies ranging from AI cloud-computing providers and suppliers to the biggest labs. Analysts say that makes Huang a potential risk to the AI industry as Nvidia investigates whether he was targeted by foreign intelligence after Huang confirmed his affair with a Chinese businesswoman accused of passing information to Beijing.

"It is hard not to read the news over the weekend as negative given it brings the stewardship of one of America's most important companies and the architect of the US AI trajectory under debate," Stacy Rasgon, analyst at Bernstein, said. "Nvidia is not an ordinary company and Jensen is not an ordinary CEO; he is Nvidia, clearly sets the long-term strategy and direction, and pulls most of the company's strings himself." VOCAL AI CHAMPION Such is Huang's spell that a casual night of fried chicken and beer in Seoul with the CEOs of Samsung and Hyundai last year sent the shares of two South Korean food companies soaring, while his endorsement of Marvell Technology as the next "trillion-dollar company" propelled the shares of the custom chipmaker to record highs. As a leading counterweight to AI skeptics, Huang has often dismissed fears of a bubble and challenged Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's apocalyptic warning that the technology could pose an existential threat to humanity. Any setback for Huang could deprive the AI industry of one of its most vocal champions who has often argued that the technology would transform everything from computing and manufacturing to healthcare and robotics. AI'S CHIP ALLOCATOR-IN-CHIEF AND A POWERFUL BOSS Huang's influence goes beyond talking up AI. He holds sway over the supply of the chips that can determine how fast AI companies spending tens of billions of dollars can grow. That status was validated by Oracle co-founder Ellison in September 2024 when he recounted a dinner at Nobu in Palo Alto. "I would describe the dinner as me and Elon begging Jensen for GPUs," Ellison told analysts. "Please take our money ... We need you to take more of our money." Huang has a firm grip on Nvidia, which he runs through an unusually flat structure, with dozens of executives reporting directly to him. However, as its fifth-largest shareholder with a roughly 3.6 per cent stake, he does not have special voting shares that give founders such as Meta Platforms' Mark Zuckerberg and SpaceX's Elon Musk majority control of their companies. "A lot of companies' organization charts, they all look the same. And it doesn't make any sense to me. The architecture of the company should reflect the environment in which it exists," Huang said on the Lex Fridman Podcast in March. He said more than 60 executives report to him, nearly all in engineering roles, including experts in memory chips, networking and graphics and central processors. Huang's family is also woven into Nvidia, with son-in-law Nico Caprez overseeing ties with neoclouds and data-center operators as vice president of global AI infrastructure growth. Huang's daughter Madison is a senior director overseeing marketing for Nvidia's physical AI products and often accompanies him on business trips, while his son Spencer works in the robotics division. NO IMMEDIATE SUCCESSOR Analysts have said Huang, who has run Nvidia since co-founding the chip designer in 1993, has no clear successor. The company, which said over the weekend Huang has the board's backing, has not disclosed a succession plan. "Jensen is not replaceable... there is no other person on the management team bench that can step in seamlessly as CEO," said long-time technology bull Dan Ives, partner and senior managing director at Yorkville Ives & Co. Besides Huang, Nvidia lists four executives on its leadership page. The best known is finance chief Colette Kress, who often represents the company at investor conferences. The others are executive vice president of worldwide field operations Nick Parker, executive vice president of operations Debora Shoquist and Tim Teter, executive vice president, general counsel and secretary.

Source: Reuters

WASHINGTON, Nov 9 : Japanese automaker Honda Motor will build a new $3 billion auto plant in central Ohio to make hybrid vehicles, creating 2,000 jobs, it said on Monday. The company said the plant will be able to produce 240,000 vehicles annually and begin production in 2029. It will increase its US auto production capacity to 1.3 million vehicles annually, and North American capacity to 1.9 million. Honda is also making a C$867 million ($613.6 million) commitment to its Canadian operations, including a C$166 million investment in its Alliston, Ontario, operations, maintaining its 4,000-strong Canadian workforce. The Canadian government said it is investing C$313 million in the Alliston project.

AUTOMAKERS FACING US TARIFFS A number of foreign automakers have announced major new investments as they face tariffs imposed by President Donald Trump's administration. Reuters reported last month that Trump's administration had promised tariff relief to Audi to help secure the plant's future. US officials told Audi executives the government plans to offer broad relief from tariffs for automakers making significant investments in US production. Morgan Stanley said the selloff looked overdone and that the ultimate impact would be a push-out of some projects from 2028 to 2029, rather than a derailing of the capex story. Brokerage HSBC said in a note that it is using last week's correction to increase its exposure to equities again, leaning into tech stocks in the US and Asia. WASHINGTON, Nov 9 : The Pentagon removed Chinese biotechnology company WuXi AppTec from its list of Chinese military companies, according to a government posting on Monday. The deputy secretary of defense made the determination in light of a federal court in Washington barring the department from enforcing the designation, the posting said. The ruling came in a lawsuit WuXi AppTec filed after the Pentagon added it to the list, saying its designation was arbitrary, capricious, unsupported by the facts and "the product of political pressure." The Pentagon expanded its blacklist of alleged "Chinese military companies" on June 8 to 188 entities.  "This decision relieves the company from further adverse consequences of the 1260H designation," WuXi AppTec said in a filing to the Hong Kong bourse on Tuesday morning, referring to the list which is kept under Section 1260H of a US defense law. "We remain committed to serving our customers and enabling the lifesaving and life-improving medicines they make for patients," the company added.

Nov 9 : SiriusXM on Monday named board member Anjali Sud, the head of Fox-owned streaming service Tubi, as its CEO, turning to a digital media veteran to help reinvigorate growth as listeners shift away from satellite radio. Here are more details: • Sud, who will take over as CEO effective January 1, 2027, has been an independent director on SiriusXM's board since March 2025 and will remain a member of the board following her appointment • She succeeds Jennifer Witz, who is stepping down after almost 25 years at the company, including nearly six as CEO

• Witz will stay on in an advisory role through the end of 2027 • Sud has led Fox Corp's Tubi since 2023 and previously was CEO of video platform Vimeo • SiriusXM is the largest US satellite radio company but has struggled to chart its future as more listeners choose streaming • SiriusXM reported third-quarter revenue of $2.15 billion last month, slightly below analysts' estimate of $2.16 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG

Source: Reuters

Nov 9 : Meta Platforms said on Monday it would expand its AI age-estimation technology globally to move millions more teens on Instagram into Teen Account protections, even if they have given birth dates showing they are adults, as the company faces lawsuits alleging its platforms harm young users. Here are more details: • Teen Accounts, available on Instagram, Facebook and Messenger, include built-in protections that automatically limit who can contact teens, the content they see and their time on the apps • Parents in the US will begin receiving Instagram notifications this month explaining how teens are placed in age-appropriate protections, Meta said

• In Australia, Meta has begun using Apple's age-range signal as an additional method to help determine users' ages. • Meta said it is continuing to roll out the technology on Facebook and will begin launching similar technology globally on Threads later this year • Meta faces multiple lawsuits over allegations that its platforms harm teens • In August, Meta struck settlements worth up to $18 billion with nearly every US state and territory to resolve lawsuits brought by attorneys general over the platforms' harm to teens • Under the settlements, Meta agreed to improve how it identifies teens and children under 13 • Meta settled with a teen plaintiff last month in a Los Angeles trial testing claims that Instagram and Facebook were designed to be addictive, causing mental health problems and an eating disorder

Source: Reuters
